question: Does the EMB-hosted Amnay River restoration EIS provide usable river fish evidence, and can its freshwater, estuary, offshore, and diet material be distinguished?

source.title: Environmental Impact Statement Report: Amnay River Restoration and Desilting Project (ARRDP), Sablayan, Occidental Mindoro
source.documentStatus: The cover labels this a 2nd draft report.
source.preparedBy: FORESTERplan Landscape Consultancy Service for City Pacific Group, Inc.
source.rightsStatus: The reviewed PDF contains no explicit open license or affirmative public-app reuse permission. Government hosting does not by itself establish rights to republish consultant-authored tables, photographs, or derivative datasets.

lowerRiverFishCatch.sourceTable: Table 2.2.19, List of Fish Species in Amnay River Caught by Locals during the Survey, August 2021
lowerRiverFishCatch.reportedArea: Amnay River project study stretch in Sablayan, Occidental Mindoro; the EIS describes a 14-km Lower Amnay River project zone elsewhere, but does not crosswalk fish to a named station.
lowerRiverFishCatch.method: Opportunistic recording of fish caught by local fishers along the project-site stretch because the river was extremely shallow; catches were photographed, short interviews were conducted, and fish were identified in a laboratory to the nearest taxon possible. Total length was measured using ImageJ.
lowerRiverFishCatch.effortOrStationCrosswalk: No fish-specific station coordinates, number of fish per taxon, sampling effort, voucher/accession roster, or fish-to-water-quality-station crosswalk was located.
lowerRiverFishCatch.tableWideIucnCell: Least Concern is printed in one cell spanning the 10 rows; no independent taxon-by-taxon IUCN verification was performed.
interpretationLimits: The EIS calls the list species, but six of its ten labels are genus-only.
The common name Nile Tilapia does not resolve Oreochromis sp. to O. niloticus.

Channa sp. is paired with Galaxiidae in the source table, while the indexed Catalog of Fishes genus entry places Channa in Channidae; the direct Catalog page returned 403, so preserve the source label and flag a family conflict without inferring a species.
Poecillia sp. is preserved exactly as printed; no spelling correction or species identity is inferred.
The report places Selar crumenophthalmus, Gazza sp., and Sardinella sp. in marine habitat and says they were caught at the river-mouth estuary; do not treat them as freshwater-reach occurrences.
Fish were not linked to the water-quality or freshwater-ecology station coordinates elsewhere in the EIS.

estuaryAndOffshoreCatch.sourceTable: Table 2.2.25, Summary of Fish Species Collected in Amnay River Estuary and its Surrounding Waters, August 2022
estuaryAndOffshoreCatch.reportedLocality: Fishers reportedly caught the fish at the river mouth and surrounding waters approximately 16 km offshore.
estuaryAndOffshoreCatch.reportedTotal: 24 species in 13 families, according to the EIS narrative.
estuaryAndOffshoreCatch.disposition: A separate estuary/coastal-offshore catch slice, not the August 2021 lower-river list. It was not extracted into a river checklist and must not be mixed with freshwater evidence.

dietReview.sourceStatement: The EIS attributes a broad diet summary to Froese and Pauly (2021): many listed fishes eat smaller fish and benthic animals; it also says Oreochromis, Osteomugil cunnesius, Poecillia, and Barbodes feed on plankton and detritus based on cited literature.
dietReview.evidenceType: Secondary-literature summary in a draft project EIS; no stomach-content analysis, prey observation, or species-by-species citation mapping is reported for Amnay fish.
dietReview.decision: Do not treat this paragraph as Amnay-specific observed diet or bait guidance. No diet assertion was admitted.

qualityAndRights.sourceCompleteness: The official EMB MIMAROPA host exposes a 13,000-plus-line PDF with a February 2023 2nd-draft cover; it is not a final EIS acceptance or project permit record.
qualityAndRights.rights: No explicit open license or public-app reuse terms were found in the reviewed PDF.
fieldQuality: The river list is opportunistic local catch, not a standardized abundance or complete checklist survey.
Taxonomic resolution is explicitly only to the nearest taxon possible, and no voucher or specimen accession list is given.
The report's 2022 estuary/offshore catches are stated by fishers and are not a freshwater river reach dataset.
The report's habitat and diet paragraphs cite secondary sources and do not provide direct local feeding observations.

decision.reason: The source is useful as a dated, local-catch research lead, but the fish method is opportunistic, six names are genus-only, one source family assignment conflicts with the Catalog of Fishes genus classification, fish are not linked to station coordinates or vouchers, and reuse permission is unverified. River, estuary, and offshore slices must remain separate.

nextAction: Continue Mindoro and MIMAROPA inland-water coverage with standardized named-waterbody surveys or specimen-backed records and explicit reuse terms. For any later Amnay admission, first obtain the EIS source/reuse status and a qualified fish-identification or voucher crosswalk; keep the 2022 estuary/offshore survey separate.

sources.supports: EIS cover and 2nd-draft date; August 2021 opportunistic lower-river method and Table 2.2.19; separate August 2022 estuary/offshore catch summary; secondary diet citations; no explicit reuse license located.
Indexed Catalog of Fishes genus record places Channa in Channidae. Direct page access returned 403, and this family crosscheck does not identify the Amnay specimen.
